'''Sir Aubrey Fiennes Trotman-Dickenson''' (12 February 1926 – 11 November 2016) was a British [[chemist]] and [[academic administrator]].

==Early life and education==
Trotman-Dickenson was born in [[Wilmslow]], [[Cheshire]] on 12 February 1926. His father, Edward Newton Trotman-Dickenson was a cotton merchant and his mother was Violet Murray, née Nicoll. He attended [[Winchester College]] and continued to study Chemistry with a scholarship to [[Balliol College, Oxford]] in 1944.<ref name=":0">{{ODNB|title=Dickenson, Sir Aubrey Fiennes Trotman- (1926–2016) |url=https://doi.org/10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.013.111566|doi=10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.013.111566 | last= Smith | first= Brian |author-link= Brian Smith (administrator) |date= 2020-01-09}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Having Graduated from Oxford, Trotman-Dickenson moved to [[Ottawa]] to work at [[National Research Council Canada]] from 1948 to 1950. He then completed an [[Imperial Chemical Industries|ICI]] Fellowship at [[University of Manchester|Manchester]],<ref name="obit - Tele">{{cite news|title=Sir Aubrey Fiennes Trotman-Dickenson, scientist and university administrator – obituary|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2016/11/25/sir-aubrey-fiennes-trotman-dickenson-scientist-university-administrator/|accessdate=2 December 2016|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=25 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230127065609/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2016/11/25/sir-aubrey-fiennes-trotman-dickenson-scientist-university-administrator/|archive-date=2023-01-27|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="obit - Cardiff uni">{{cite web|title=Sir Aubrey Fiennes Trotman-Dickenson|url=http://www.cardiff.ac.uk/obituaries/obituary/sir-aubrey-fiennes-trotman-dickenson|website=[[Cardiff University]]|publisher=|accessdate=2 December 2016|date=2016}}</ref> where he also earned his PhD in 1952.<ref>{{Citebook |url=https://archive.org/details/registerof18511958univuoft |title=University of Manchester: Register of graduates and holders of diplomas and certificates, 1851—1958 |publisher=[[Manchester University Press]] |year=1959 |location=[[Manchester]] |page=667 |via=[[Internet Archive]]}}</ref> He worked as a [[lecturer]] in chemistry at the [[University of Edinburgh]], where he received a DSc in 1957 for a portfolio of works titled, ''The kinetics of elementary reactions''.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Trotman-Dickenon |first=A. F. |title=The kinetics of elementary reactions |date=1957 |degree=DSc |publisher=[[University of Edinburgh]] |url=https://era.ed.ac.uk/items/810185b9-0e36-441c-aaf6-69ba8c9301aa}}</ref> He was made [[Professor]] and chair of Chemistry at [[University College of Wales, Aberystwyth]] by the age of 34. He was appointed [[Principal (academia)|Principal]] of the [[University of Wales Institute of Science and Technology]] (UWIST) in 1968 and continued as Principal of its successor, [[University of Wales College of Cardiff]], from 1988 to 1993. He additionally served as the Vice-Chancellor of the [[University of Wales]] for three terms: 1975 to 1977, 1983 to 1985, and 1991 to 1993.<ref name="obit - Cardiff uni" /><ref name="obit - THE">{{cite news|last1=Grove|first1=Jack|title=Aubrey Trotman-Dickenson, 1926–2016|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/people/obituary-aubrey-trotman-dickenson-1926-2016|accessdate=2 December 2016|work=Times Higher Education|date=1 December 2016}}</ref><ref name="Who's Who 2017">{{Who's Who|id=U38071|title=TROTMAN-DICKENSON, Sir Aubrey (Fiennes)|date=2017-12-01}}</ref>

==Honours==
In the [[1989 Queen's Birthday Honours]], it was announced that Trotman-Dickenson had been appointed a [[Knight Bachelor]] and therefore granted the [[title]] ''[[sir]]'', in recognition of his service as Principal of University of Wales, College of Cardiff.<ref name="LG 16 June 1989">{{London Gazette |issue=51772 |date=16 June 1989 |pages=1–2  |supp=y }}</ref> On 5 December 1989, he was knighted by [[Queen Elizabeth II]] during a ceremony at [[Buckingham Palace]].<ref name="LG 5 January 1990">{{London Gazette |issue=52009 |date=5 January 1990 |page=221 }}</ref>

In 1963, Trotman-Dickenson was the [[Tilden Prize|Tilden Lecturer]] for the [[Chemical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tilden Prizes Previous Winners|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/TildenPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|accessdate=2 December 2016|date=2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729224013/http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/TildenPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp|archive-date=2017-07-29|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1995, he was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary]] [[Doctor of Laws]] (LLD) degree by the [[University of Wales]].<ref name="Who's Who 2017" />

== Personal life and politics ==
On 11 July 1953 Trotman-Dickenson married economist [[Danusia, Lady Trotman-Dickenson|Donata Irena (Danusia) Hewell]] and they had three children together.<ref name=":0" />

He was a member of the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] before eventually joining the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Political focus: 'People are moving towards the Lib Dems' |work=[[South Wales Echo]] |date=2002-11-05 |page=25 |url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A94007564/STND?u=wikipedia&sid=bookmark-STND&xid=4fedd18a |via=[[Gale (publisher)|Gale]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-02-23 |title=Sir Aubrey Fiennes Trotman-Dickenson |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/article/sir-aubrey-fiennes-trotman-dickenson-zt9kxzblf |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> He stood as a Lib Dem candidate in the [[2003 South Gloucestershire Council election]] though he did not succeed in securing a seat.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Local Elections Handbook 2003|first=Colin|last= Rallings|first2= Michael|last2= Thrasher|author-link=Colin Rallings|author2-link= Michael Thrasher|url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/07/Local-Elections-Handbook-2003-complete.pdf|isbn=0-948858-35-4|publisher= Local Government Chronicle Elections Centre|location=[[University of Plymouth]]|page=78|chapter=Unitary Council Election Results}}</ref>

Trotman-Dickenson died on 11 November 2016, at his home in [[Siston#Siston Court|Siston Court]] as a result of heart failure. Lady Trotman-Dickenson died on 28 June 2024, at the age of 95.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-07-07 |title=Births, marriages and deaths: July 8, 2024 |url=https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/births-marriages-and-deaths-july-8-2024-mxmdqwwcx |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=[[The Times]] |language=en-GB}}</ref>
